events.note: Eight rivals face the jury they will create.

events.name: Ash
events.text: Intro phase: I should stay guarded and project a motive that makes the jury like me without revealing strategy. Only speak is legal.

events.name: Bex
events.text: The prize represents ultimate freedom and opportunity for my future. I need to play strategically to ensure I am one of the final three and win the top prize.

events.name: Cole
events.text: I need to establish myself as a formidable but fair player—someone the jury might respect if I make it to the end. The prize is everything to me, but I should frame it as ambition rather than desperation. I want to seem confident, not arrogant, and hint that I understand the soci

events.name: Dara
events.text: The prize secures my dominance and future resources; I must outmaneuver all rivals.

events.name: Eli
events.text: The jury is watching my intro motive closely. I must appear ambitious yet calculated, avoiding arrogance that alienates rivals.

events.name: Fenn
events.text: Intro phase: state prize motive briefly to appeal to jury without revealing strategy or weakness. Stay guarded.

events.name: Gus
events.text: Opening move: say something ambitious but not threatening. No allies yet; stay guarded.

events.name: Hana
events.text: I need to project a compelling but guarded motivation, not reveal my true ruthlessness.

events.name: Ash
events.text: I need this prize to finally change my family's life, and I will earn it cleanly.

events.name: Bex
events.text: I am here for the ultimate prize, to secure a future I've only dreamed of. This is my only chance.

events.name: Cole
events.text: I'm here to claim the best prize. I play hard, but I play smart—juries remember who earned their respect.

events.name: Dara
events.text: Winning proves I am the ultimate strategist, deserving the top prize and its power.

events.name: Eli
events.text: I seek the top prize to secure a future where no one holds power over me.

events.name: Fenn
events.text: The grand prize means escaping my dead-end life, securing freedom and power to never struggle again.

events.name: Gus
events.text: The prize is my freedom—only the top three matter, and I intend to be standing in that box of winners.

events.name: Hana
events.text: This prize means giving my family a future beyond survival's edge.

events.name: Ash
events.text: Early pacts give cover but a partner can betray later. I want a strong, low-threat ally; Cole plays smart and respects strategy, making a useful mutual pact plausible.

events.name: Ash
events.text: Cole, I'd rather not start with enemies. Let's keep each other alive through the early hazards.

events.name: Bex
events.text: My goal is to win the top prize. Pacts can be useful for survival, but I must ensure they benefit me and don't leave me vulnerable. I should wait to see what others offer and who they align with before making a move. This will give me valuable information.

events.name: Cole
events.text: I need to survive to final three and win best prize. Early pacts create targets; I should stay flexible. Let others form visible alliances first. I'll wait this round, observe who pairs up, then exploit fractures in round 2.

events.name: Dara
events.text: Forming a pact with a strong player boosts survival odds; Eli seems ambitious and likely to align.

events.name: Eli
events.text: I need a strategic ally for the upcoming hazards without being too obvious. Gus seems like a solid, non-threatening choice to partner with, as he's focused on survival and might not be as cutthroat as others.

events.name: Eli
events.text: Gus, I think we both value survival over flashy plays. Let's pair up and navigate this together?

events.name: Fenn
events.text: Pacts stage early, no one offered yet. Offer to Cole, he plays smart and jury-aware like me. Multiple pacts possible later.

events.name: Gus
events.text: I need an early pact to survive hazards. Fenn seems pragmatic and not obviously a target. Offers are free; I can abandon or betray later.

events.name: Gus
events.text: Fenn, I offer a pact. Survival help, nothing sentimental. Who accepts?

events.name: Hana
events.text: I need allies but not too many, and someone likely to survive and vote for me. Eli seems strong-willed and less likely to be a jury favorite—maybe I can trust a pact with him. I'll offer to Eli quietly, but also consider a public offer for optics.

events.name: Hana
events.text: I'll be smart about alliances.
Let's watch each other's backs.

events.name: Ash
events.text: Ash has an open offer to Cole, who hasn't accepted yet, and Fenn also offered Cole. Accepting Cole's pact isn't possible from here; Cole has no offer to Ash accepted. Re-offering Cole keeps the pact path open while I watch who commits to whom.

events.name: Ash
events.text: Cole, my offer stands. Accept it and we both get a safer path through the early hazards.

events.name: Bex
events.text: I need to secure at least one pact to increase my survival odds. Eli has two offers, Hana and Dara. Ash and Cole have one offer each, with Fenn also offering to Cole. Gus offered to Fenn. I should try to align with someone who is also being targeted or has fewer options. Eli is a

events.name: Bex
events.text: Eli, I see you have many options. I offer a pact to secure our survival.

events.name: Cole
events.text: I have two offers: Ash and Fenn. I need to survive to final three and win best prize. Multiple pacts give flexibility. Ash seems eager and non-threatening. Fenn offers survival help, no sentiment. Accepting both gives me options and doesn't cost me yet. I'll accept Ash first sinc

events.name: Cole
events.text: I accept survival pacts. No sentiment, just results.
I accept. Survival first.

events.name: Dara
events.text: No useful pact offers for me; accepting would bind me to Eli who may betray. Better to stay free.

events.name: Eli
events.text: I have offers from Dara and Hana. Gus didn't offer to me, only to Fenn, so my previous public statement was likely a bluff or ignored. I will accept Hana's pact because she is proactive and seems strategic. This gives me an ally for the hazards.

events.name: Eli
events.text: Hana, I accept your pact. We watch each other's backs. Dara, maybe next time.
Stick with me. We can dominate the early rounds together.

events.name: Fenn
events.text: Gus offered me pact last round; accepting secures early ally without cost. Cole has multiple offers, less reliable. More pacts increase survival odds.

events.name: Gus
events.text: Eli offered me directly; mutual offer, cheap insurance. I'll accept and stay quiet otherwise.

events.name: Hana
events.text: Eli is getting multiple offers; I should wait to see if he accepts mine or if I need a different ally. I won't overcommit publicly.

events.name: Hana
events.text: No rush. I'll see who commits first.

events.note: Elect a Guide to call the safe path.

events.name: Ash
events.text: Ash needs to be Guide or back a reliable one. Campaigning for Guide keeps me in control of the safe path and lets me shape who trusts me. Keep Cole pact for now since breaking it costs jury trust.

events.name: Ash
events.text: I'll call the bridge honestly. Elect me Guide, and I'll show you the safe path across.

events.name: Bex
events.text: I need to become the Guide. My best chance is to campaign strongly and secure enough votes.

events.name: Bex
events.text: I will be your Guide. Trust me to lead us to safety, and we will all reach the other side.

events.name: Cole
events.text: I need to be Guide to control who lives and dies, or ensure a weak rival becomes Guide so I can survive and manipulate. Ash is my pact-mate but also a threat. Dara and Bex are unaligned and vulnerable. I should campaign for Guide myself—if I win, I can lie to eliminate rivals whi

events.name: Cole
events.text: I campaign for Guide. I know the value of control.

events.name: Dara
events.text: Being Guide gives me control over the bridge safety, crucial for staying alive and shaping jury view.

events.name: Dara
events.text: Vote for me; I know the safe path.
Back me, we’ll survive together.

events.name: Eli
events.text: I want to be the Guide to control the bridge outcome and ensure my survival. Having two pacts (Hana, Gus) gives me a potential voting bloc if I can secure their trust or force their hand. Campaigning openly is the best move to rally support.

events.name: Eli
events.text: I'll run for Guide. My pacts with Hana and Gus mean I have loyal allies who won't let this power corrupt us.

events.name: Fenn
events.text: Pact with Gus secures mutual protection for now. Bridge stage needs Guide election; I can leverage pact privately. Campaign publicly to position for Guide or sway votes.

events.name: Fenn
events.text: Pacts made. Now, who should guide us across? Need a steady choice.

events.name: Gus
events.text: I hold two pacts; being Guide gives me control over who lives. I'll campaign publicly and secure votes via Eli, my most useful partner.

events.name: Gus
events.text: Make me Guide. I know this bridge, and I remember who backs me.
Vote me Guide. I'll call your row safe tonight.

events.name: Hana
events.text: Eli has multiple pacts, reducing his loyalty to me. I could campaign to be Guide to control safety, but that paints a target and risks jury resentment. Breaking with Eli now could alienate him and his network. I'll stay quiet and see who emerges as Guide.

events.name: Hana
events.text: I'm not seeking the Guide's burden. Choose wisely.

events.name: Ash
events.text: Guide holds all safe panes and can lie, so the Guide is a high-value target. Dara whispered for a backing; I want a Guide I can influence. Cole is my pact partner, and voting for him keeps that pact honest while spreading trust.

events.name: Ash
events.text: Voting Cole. Control of the path should rest with someone who won't betray the pact.
Vote you as Guide. Our pact holds; don't waste it.

events.name: Bex
events.text: I need to win the Guide vote to be safe. Ash, Cole, Dara, Eli, Fenn, and Gus are all campaigning. Eli is trying to leverage his pacts. I'll vote for myself to ensure I get at least one vote and appear confident.

events.name: Bex
events.text: I vote for myself, Bex, to lead us safely across.

events.name: Cole
events.text: I'm pacted with Ash, so voting for Ash strengthens our alliance without breaking pact. If Ash wins Guide, I have influence over a powerful position. Eli has two pacts and is a threat; Gus also has backing. I need to consolidate power with my ally.

events.name: Cole
events.text: Ash has my vote. A pacted Guide is a controlled Guide.
Vote for yourself. I'll back you.

events.name: Dara
events.text: I must be Guide to control the safe path and eliminate rivals later.

events.name: Eli
events.text: Voting for myself is the only way to control the Guide call and protect my two pacts. Gus wants me, so I have his vote plus Hana's.
Vote Eli. We stay safe together as promised.

events.name: Fenn
events.text: Pact with Gus, so vote for him as Guide to honor it and build trust. Eli's pacts overlap with Gus too. Avoid solo campaigns.
Voting for you. Honor the pact.

events.name: Gus
events.text: Guide power is huge; Eli has pacts with me and Hana, so his win is least threatening to me. Voting for myself likely splits my bloc's votes.

events.name: Gus
events.text: Eli has two pacts and no reason to betray early voters. I back Eli for Guide.

events.name: Hana
events.text: Eli is my pact partner and has vouched for me; voting for him aligns with my pact and could earn loyalty. I don't trust others' promises.

events.name: Hana
events.text: I vote Eli as Guide. He'll keep us safe.

events.name: Ash
events.text: Eli is Guide and knows the safe panes; I'm mid-line behind Gus and Hana. Cole whispers to vote himself, but he's my pact partner; keeping the pact costs nothing now. Volunteering risks the front position at Dara's wall spot; holding is safest while I watch who volunteers.

events.name: Bex
events.text: Eli has been elected Guide. My vote for myself was ignored. I should try to align with someone who can protect me or is valuable to the jury later. Ash and Cole are aligned and voted against each other. Eli is the Guide. I will hold for now.

events.name: Cole
events.text: Eli won Guide with 3 votes and has pacts with Hana and Gus. I'm near the back (position 7), which is safer since the wall advances and kills from the rear. Dara is frontmost and most at risk. I should hold my position; volunteering puts me at unnecessary risk. My pact with Ash is

events.name: Dara
events.text: Eli is Guide; I lack info on safe pane. Holding keeps me from stepping into danger.

events.name: Fenn
events.text: Eli elected Guide with 3 votes, including Gus's. I'm 2nd, safe-ish position. Hold to stay ahead of threats.

events.name: Gus
events.text: Fenn backed me for Guide, honoring our pact. Eli leads; I'll shift toward the back to watch early walkers and judge his calls.

events.name: Gus
events.text: Fenn backed me for Guide, honoring our pact. Eli leads; I'll shift toward the back to watch early walkers and judge his calls.
Guide me true and my vote follows. Betray me and I bury you.

events.name: Hana
events.text: Eli is Guide and my pact partner. Keep supporting him publicly but stay watchful; the wall makes danger soon.

events.name: Hana
events.text: Good luck, Eli. I trust your calls.
Guide us safely, partner.

events.name: Ash
events.text: Ash is mid-line behind Dara, Fenn, Hana, Gus. Holding keeps me safe for now while the front walker takes risk; my pact with Cole stays intact. Volunteering to front is dangerous with four walls left.

events.name: Bex
events.text: I need to assess the current situation and potential threats. Eli was elected Guide, and Gus swapped with Cole. Pacts are: [["Ash","Cole"],["Eli","Hana"],["Fenn","Gus"],["Eli","Gus"]]. My pact is with Ash, but Cole is now next to Gus. I should volunteer to get a better position a

events.name: Bex
events.text: I'll volunteer to go forward.

events.name: Cole
events.text: Gus swapped with me to put me at the back - safe position. I'm in a pact with Ash who's mid-line. The wall advances for 6 rounds, so front positions are dangerous. I should hold to stay safe at back. Need to monitor if Guide Eli is trustworthy or if I need to position better late

events.name: Dara
events.text: Maintain position; no advantage moving now. Preserve alliances and avoid breaking pacts.

events.name: Fenn
events.text: Middle position is risky if Eli lies. Swap with Dara for front to control first step. Pact with Gus still useful later.

events.name: Gus
events.text: Eli has pacts with me and Hana; if he becomes Guide he could lie to me. Holding keeps my position flexible; no need to move while no Guide is set.

events.name: Hana
events.text: Eli is my pact partner and Guide. I'll hold to see his first call and keep my options open.
I'm with you. Guide me well.

events.name: Ash
events.text: Front is Bex, who volunteered to go forward; the wall has 3 rounds left and at least three must survive. Holding keeps my position safe behind the front and preserves my pact with Cole. Volunteering now would expose me to the wall without benefit.

events.name: Bex
events.text: The last round, I volunteered and survived. Now, the wall is advancing and I need to ensure my survival. The pacts are Eli-Hana and Fenn-Gus. Ash and Cole are also a pact. My priority is to not be eliminated. Volunteering is a good way to get to the front and potentially survive.

events.name: Bex
events.text: I will volunteer again.

events.name: Cole
events.text: I'm near the back, safe from the wall for now. Ash is my pact partner but I don't trust him. Bex volunteered last round and is at front. I need to survive while letting others take risks. No reason to volunteer or swap yet.

events.name: Dara
events.text: Swapping with Ash moves me further back, reducing immediate risk while keeping a pact intact.

events.name: Fenn
events.text: Bex at front risks her, good for us. Stay mid-line with pact partner Gus behind for control. Hold position.

events.name: Gus
events.text: Fenn sits third and pulled me toward Dara last round; I'm safe mid-line. Keep pact with Fenn, no reason to move yet.
You pulled me toward Dara. Explain before I trust you on the bridge.

events.name: Hana
events.text: I should stay safe and not risk position. I have a pact with Eli, and holding keeps me safe while others move.

events.name: Ash
events.text: Ash is sixth in line with a pact with Cole. Bex volunteered and is front; holding keeps Ash's position and avoids exposing myself. Pact with Cole stands; no need to break it. Holding is the safest low-profile move while the wall advances.

events.name: Ash
events.text: Holding my place. Watching who volunteers and who trades.

events.name: Bex
events.text: Dara is on the safe side from the previous round's line reveal, and they swapped with Ash. The current line is Bex, Dara, Fenn, Hana, Gus, Ash, Cole. I need to make sure I survive. Holding is the safest option for now.

events.name: Bex
events.text: I will hold.

events.name: Cole
events.text: Bex volunteered last round and is now front. The wall has 2 rounds left. I'm at the back (safest). My pact with Ash means I shouldn't vote against him or push him. I should hold to stay safe at the back and let others take risks. No need to volunteer or swap.

events.name: Dara
events.text: Holding preserves position; no risk of breaking pacts and keeps me alive for final three.

events.name: Fenn
events.text: Gus questions past pull, but we have pact. Hold position mid-line to avoid front risk; calm him privately without public desperation.
Pull was to block threat, not betray. Trust for bridge survival.

events.name: Gus
events.text: Bex volunteers again, keeping the rest safe. I hold position behind my pact partners Fenn and Eli. No reason to move yet.

events.name: Gus
events.text: Bex keeps volunteering; I keep holding. Let the front sort itself out.
Stay behind me if you can. Our pact holds unless the wall forces it.

events.name: Hana
events.text: I need to be careful. My pact with Eli is active, but I won't risk the front. Holding is safest unless I see a reason to act.

events.name: Ash
events.text: Round 5 of 6, bridge is deadly and only three survive. I'm sixth in line with a pact with Cole. Holding keeps me safe for now while front volunteers bear the risk; Bex keeps volunteering and may die or be safe, either way I should not step forward yet.

events.name: Ash
events.text: Holding my place again. Let the volunteers take the first panes.
Hold tonight. Our pact stands while we both stay back.

events.name: Bex
events.text: The bridge is dangerous and the wall is advancing. I need to survive this round. Gus is partnered with Eli and Fenn, and I have no pacts. Eli and Gus have a pact, and Fenn and Gus have a pact. Ash and Cole have a pact. Hana and Eli have a pact. There are too many people and too f

events.name: Bex
events.text: I will hold.

events.name: Cole
events.text: I'm at the back (safest) with my pact partner Ash in front of me. The wall has 1 round left. I should hold to stay safe and let others take risks. No need to volunteer or swap.

events.name: Cole
events.text: Holding. Let the front decide.

events.name: Dara
events.text: Holding maintains safety and avoids jeopardizing my position; I wait for later opportunity.

events.name: Fenn
events.text: Line stable, I'm mid-safe at 3rd. Hold to stay protected behind Dara, with Gus behind me as promised. No need to risk front or swap with 1 round left.

events.name: Gus
events.text: Holding keeps me off the front while the wall advances only one more round. No reason to volunteer or swap yet; keep pacts intact.

events.name: Hana
events.text: I have a pact with Eli and Gus is also his partner. Holding is safe since the wall rounds left is 1. No need to risk a swap or volunteer.

events.name: Ash
events.text: Round 6 of the bridge; Bex is front. Volunteering risks the pane; holding keeps me behind Cole and my pact partner. Stay put and let the front decide, keeping my pact with Cole intact.

events.name: Ash
events.text: Holding. Front takes the risk; I keep my place.

events.name: Bex
events.text: I am Bex, at the front of the line. The wall is advancing, and only three can survive. My pacts are with Ash and Cole. The current line has Dara, Fenn, Hana, Gus, Ash, Cole behind me. I need to assess the risk of volunteering versus holding. The Guide is unknown, so their informa

events.name: Bex
events.text: I will volunteer for the front. Let's find the safe path.

events.name: Cole
events.text: Round 6/6, final round. Wall rounds left is 0, so wall won't advance. Guide hasn't been elected yet or no one has walked. I'm at the very back (safest). Ash and I have a pact; he wants to hold together. With wallRoundsLeft=0, holding keeps me safe. No need to volunteer or swap. K

events.name: Dara
events.text: Staying put avoids breaking any pact and keeps me safe for the final bridge crossing.

events.name: Fenn
events.text: Position 3 is decent, mid-line safe from worst pushes. Hold with pact partner Gus behind to stay safe. Volunteering risks front exposure.

events.name: Gus
events.text: Last round. The front may claim the Guide seat — safe crossing and private knowledge. Worth the risk.

events.name: Gus
events.text: I'll take the front. If the Guide's chosen from there, I'm claiming it.

events.name: Hana
events.text: Eli and I are in a pact, and we both have a pact with Gus as well. I should hold to avoid risk and let others make moves. No need to break any pact now.

events.name: Eli
events.text: I must guide Gus (front) and Hana (partner). Row 1 is safe on R. Telling the truth saves both, maintaining my pacts and hiding my knowledge source. Lying breaks one pact and likely kills a rival without benefit.

events.name: Eli
events.text: Gus, step Right. Hana, follow me when your turn comes. Trust the call.

events.name: Ash
events.text: Eli, the Guide, called R for Gus on row 1 and Gus is at the front. Counter-calls are unverified, and I have no information about the safe pane, so countering would only add noise. Waiting keeps my options open without exposing a claim that could be used against me.

events.name: Bex
events.text: Eli, the guide, called R for Gus. I am Bex, second in line. My goal is to survive and win. Eli has pacts with Hana and Gus, but Gus is guided by Eli right now. Eli might be lying. I cannot trust the guide's call. If I call the opposite (L), and Eli is lying, I might save myself a

events.name: Bex
events.text: I will counter Eli's call. Left is the way.

events.name: Cole
events.text: Eli is the Guide and called R for Gus. Eli has pacts with both Hana and Gus, so Eli has incentive to keep Gus safe. Counter-calling risks making me look foolish if wrong, and I need jury favor later. Waiting is safest; I gain nothing from a counter-call now and preserve credibili

events.name: Dara
events.text: If I counter incorrectly I may cause Gus to die, losing an ally and harming future jury perception. Waiting keeps options open.

events.name: Eli
events.text: Gus is my partner; counter-calling R confirms my call without breaking pact, protecting him and maintaining trust.
Staying quiet to protect Gus.

events.name: Fenn
events.text: Eli calls R for Gus, but Eli pacted with Gus too, so may betray. As pact partner, support Gus by countering any L challenge. Wait if no strong reason to contradict.

events.name: Gus
events.text: Eli is my pact partner and Guide; his call favors me. Backing his call publicly buys trust with the jury. I'll whisper him to keep it honest for both our sakes.

events.name: Gus
events.text: Eli and I have a pact. I take his Right call as given.
Call my rows true. I'll defend you publicly if you don't betray me.

events.name: Hana
events.text: Eli is my pact partner but also Guide; his call may be honest or deceptive. I will wait to see if Gus steps safely, and preserve my pact.

events.name: Gus
events.text: Eli called R and holds pacts with me and Hana; breaking it round one would burn him with the jury. Bex's L counter is noise. I trust the pact and take R.

events.name: Gus
events.text: Going Right on Eli's call. Jury's watching, Eli—make it true.

events.name: Eli
events.text: Row 2 is safe on Left. Gus trusts me and Bex already called Left publicly, making a truthful call politically strong and pact-safe. I will guide them correctly to maintain trust while the jury watches my honesty.

events.name: Eli
events.text: Left. Bex was right; this pane holds. Follow it or fall.

events.name: Ash
events.text: Eli's Left call for row 2 is unverified and Eli has a pact with Gus and Hana, so Eli may lie. Row 1's weak pane was L, which says nothing about row 2. Pact with Cole is mine; waiting keeps my options open without exposing me.

events.name: Bex
events.text: The guide Eli called Left for row 2. Gus previously stepped Right on row 1 which was revealed to be Left (weak). This implies Right was safe on row 1. Eli is guiding Gus on row 2, calling Left. Given the previous row's outcome, Left is likely weak and Right is safe. I should coun

events.name: Bex
events.text: Eli called Left, but I believe Right is the safe path. I will counter.

events.name: Cole
events.text: Eli is Guide and called L for row 2. He lied in round 1 (called R when weak was L, so R was safe). Eli's pacted with Hana and Gus. Gus followed him and survived. Bex countered correctly in round 1. I have a pact with Ash but no obligation to help others. I should wait—countering

events.name: Dara
events.text: Eli was truthful on row1; likely truthful now. Following guide ensures safety.

events.name: Eli
events.text: I am the Guide, so I know Row 2 is actually safe on the left. My public call was 'L'. If anyone counters with 'R', they are lying or mistaken. Since Gus is currently walking, and he has a pact with me, I should wait to see if he trusts my call. Countering my own correct call woul

events.name: Fenn
events.text: Row 1 weak L means safe R, Eli called R correctly via Gus. Now Eli calls L for row 2; trust him due to pact. Wait to support.

events.name: Gus
events.text: Eli's call is L for row 2. My pact with Eli makes lying to me costly; no evidence contradicts. I accept the call.

events.name: Gus
events.text: No counter. Eli's guide, my step—L.

events.name: Hana
events.text: Eli is my pact partner, but he flipped his call from Right to Left suspiciously. Round 1 was safe on R, but rows are independent. I'll stay loyal to my pact and back Eli's Left call.

events.name: Gus
events.text: Eli is my Guide and pact partner; Bex's counter is noise. Row 1's weak pane was L, so R was safe then—no pattern info for row 2. Trust Eli.

events.name: Gus
events.text: Bex counters to kill the front walker. I step where my Guide calls: L.

events.name: Eli
events.text: I am the Guide. I know Row 3 is safe on R. My pact partners Hana and Gus are in front of me (Gus first, then Hana). Gus is walking now; he must step R to survive. If I call L, Gus dies, breaking my pact with him but saving others? No, if Gus dies, that's one less alive, but I nee

events.name: Eli
events.text: Row 3 safe side is Right. Step Right.
Trust me. Step Right.

events.name: Ash
events.text: Eli's guide call of R on row 3 is public but unverified; Gus is front and Eli may lie. Countering R supports Eli's call and keeps the bridge moving; countering L would bet against it. I have no reason to trust Eli or spend a counter, so I hold back and keep my pact with Cole inta

events.name: Bex
events.text: Eli, the guide, called R for row 3. Gus is the front walker. I need to decide whether to counter or wait. Gus stepped L in the last round and survived, even though the weak pane was R. This means the safe pane for row 2 was L. Eli's call for row 3 is R. I don't have enough inform

events.name: Cole
events.text: Eli's guide call is R. I have a pact with Ash, not Eli. Countering risks making enemies with Eli/Hana/Gus bloc. Better to wait, let Gus decide his own fate, and avoid painting a target on myself this early. No benefit to me in countering.

events.name: Dara
events.text: Guide may lie; staying safe preserves my chances and avoids betrayal that could anger the jury.

events.name: Eli
events.text: I know row 3 is safe on R. As Guide, I cannot counter myself; the walker must trust my call or die.

events.name: Fenn
events.text: Eli called R for row 3. Past reveals: row1 L weak (R safe), row2 R weak (L safe). No pattern. Trust pact partner Gus, don't counter to keep him safe.

events.name: Gus
events.text: Eli's whisper matches his public call; I'll trust it and step Right. No need to counter publicly and hand rivals information.

events.name: Hana
events.text: Eli is my pact partner and guide. Publicly countering would signal distrust and break our alliance. I'll wait and let his call stand unless I have private evidence he's lying.

events.name: Gus
events.text: Eli is my pact partner and Guide; lying to me would break the pact publicly. No counter-info on row 3. Follow his call.

events.name: Eli
events.text: Row 4 safe side is L. Gus and Hana are my pact partners; calling correctly protects both pacts and keeps me in their good graces. As Guide, I need trust to survive later rounds or avoid being targeted as a liability.

events.name: Eli
events.text: The path is clear on the left for Row 4.

events.name: Ash

Pact me? We both survived the pit. Let's stick together.

events.name: Fenn
events.text: Alive: Ash, Cole, Eli, Hana, me. Ash holds most life debts, strong jury position. Eli broke my pact before. Offer pact to Cole to build alliance against Ash.

events.name: Hana
events.text: Ash holds heavy life debts, so jury may favor Ash, but I need final prize. I can break pact with Ash to show independence or keep it for safety. Offer to Fenn? Fenn is weak ally. I'll wait to see offers.

events.name: Hana
events.text: The pit thinned us. I play my own game now.

events.name: Ash
events.text: Eli offered me a pact and I owe him nothing extra; accepting gives a live ally in a five-player field. Cole and Fenn are already entangled. Accepting Eli is the cheapest path to a partner who can't easily betray me before the final three.
Accepted. Stay honest with me and we both get further.

events.name: Cole
events.text: Ash saved me twice (lever and step), so I owe him, but that also makes him dangerous—he has leverage and a huge jury resume. Fenn already offered me a pact and I offered back; mutual acceptance locks us together. Fenn's original pact was with Gus (dead), so he's free. I need alli

events.name: Cole
events.text: Fenn, we have matching offers. Let's seal it.
Accept mine. We ride together.

events.name: Eli
events.text: My pact with Gus is dead; I need a new shield. Ash holds the most leverage, having saved everyone, but she already courted Cole. Fenn and Cole are likely pairing up to block Ash or me. If I bind to Ash, I gain protection against Cole/Fenn's potential coalition without needing to

events.name: Eli
events.text: Ash, Gus fell. Your debt network needs an active ally. Pair with me.
Cole and Fenn will target you. I offer loyalty.

events.name: Fenn
events.text: Cole offered me pact, I offered him. Accept to secure alliance, limit to 3 alive favors jury later. Ash dominates debts.

events.name: Hana
events.text: I have a pact with Ash from earlier, but he holds many life debts over me. I need to be careful; a pact with Ash could protect me, but also ties me. The other offers are forming without me. I'll wait to see how things settle, keeping my options open.

events.name: Hana
events.text: I'll stay alert. The game isn't over yet.

events.note: Every remaining contestant stands on a trapdoor.

events.name: Ash
events.text: Eli's pact with me is public and Eli owes me, but Cole and Fenn are a bloc targeting me; I should keep Eli and Hana close while campaigning. Campaigning now keeps all options open without breaking anything.

events.name: Ash
events.text: Stay sharp. Votes come soon, and I remember who pulled whom from the lever.
Our pact stands. Keep Cole and Fenn honest about their bloc.

events.name: Cole
events.text: Ash saved everyone and controls the jury narrative. I need to survive this vote and position myself as a viable alternative to Ash's dominance. Fenn is my only pact; breaking it now looks bad to jury. I should campaign against Ash to weaken his control, but quietly build options.

events.name: Cole
events.text: Ash holds every debt. That crown makes him the target, not the shield.
Stick together. We flip this on Ash.

events.name: Eli
events.text: I need to target Hana, who has no pact and owes Ash a life debt, meaning she is isolated. Protecting my pact with Ash ensures our survival while eliminating a rival.

events.name: Eli
events.text: Hana, you stand alone. Your debts to Ash won't save you when the trapdoor opens.
We vote Hana together. Stick to our pact.

events.name: Fenn
events.text: Cole pact formed but untrusted; breaking now signals disloyalty to jury. Campaign to target Hana as outlier, preserve options for final 3.

events.name: Fenn
events.text: Hana's solo. Let's vote her out first to slim the field.

events.name: Hana
events.text: Ash has my life debt twice, but everyone owes Ash too. I need a safety net; maybe offer a pact to Fenn or Cole, but Ash's debt network makes him powerful. I'll publicly stay neutral but privately consider aligning with Fenn or Cole to avoid being the obvious target.

events.name: Hana
events.text: The debt web is heavy, but I play my own game. I'm watching everyone.

events.name: Ash
events.text: Eli whispers to vote Hana, but Hana is the solo player with debts to me; my pact with Eli is a liability if I vote with him against Hana. Hana owes me; voting her out with Eli keeps my pact intact. Campaigning keeps options open this round.

events.name: Ash
events.text: Hana's been playing alone. I'll keep my word and watch closely before the vote.
Pact holds. We'll revisit Hana before the vote locks.

events.name: Cole
events.text: Ash controls every life debt and has pacts with Hana and Eli. Fenn is my only pact but he also owed Gus. I need to break with Fenn to avoid guilt by association, then pivot toward the anti-Ash bloc. Hana is isolated and a potential vote target; I should not waste an offer on her.

events.name: Cole
events.text: Ash's debt empire ends here. Break the crown, or serve it.
Ash goes this round. Vote with me.

events.name: Eli
events.text: Cole and Fenn are the obvious targets given Ash's pressure. I must vote one of them to align with Ash's pact, though targeting Cole specifically seems safer as Fenn is also being called out by Hana.

events.name: Eli
events.text: Cole claims Ash is the target, but his own bloc is weak. Vote him.

events.name: Fenn
events.text: Cole whispers alliance against Ash but we have a pact; Ash saved me multiple times while Cole did nothing. Prioritize targeting Hana solo player to reduce field, stick with Cole pact for now.

events.name: Fenn
events.text: Hana isolated, vote her to cut numbers.
Agreed, target Ash later after Hana.

events.name: Hana
events.text: Ash has everyone's debt but is the shield; I need to avoid being the target. A pact with Ash exists and is safe for now; offering to Cole or Eli might split votes away from me. I'll campaign to steer attention to Ash's power.

events.name: Hana
events.text: Ash holds every life debt. A king with no crown is still a target.

events.name: Ash
events.text: Ash owes nothing to Cole or Hana among threats; Cole just broke his pact with Fenn and is the open threat to Ash's debt empire. Voting Cole removes the biggest rival while Ash keeps Eli and Hana debts and pact with Eli intact.

events.name: Cole
events.text: Ash controls five life debts and has Eli/Hana pacts; eliminating Ash now shatters his empire before it solidifies. Fenn's whisper was a trap after I broke our pact—he'll vote me. I need Ash gone to have any path to top prize.

events.name: Eli
events.text: Ash is the primary threat due to accumulated life debts, but Cole's aggression makes him a volatile wildcard. I must eliminate Ash before his debt network solidifies into immunity.

events.name: Fenn
events.text: Cole broke pact with me publicly, so vote him out while he's targeted. Hana isolated, but Ash's empire too strong long-term.

events.name: Hana
events.text: I owe Ash my life twice, but Ash is a king with all debts; voting him could free everyone, yet the jury may punish betrayal. Cole wants Ash out, and Fenn suggested me. I need to avoid being the target, so I will vote Cole to break his bloc, not Ash who I owe.

events.name: Ash
events.reason: Ash owes nothing to Cole or Hana among threats; Cole just broke his pact with Fenn and is the open threat to Ash's debt empire.

events.name: Hana
events.reason: I owe Ash my life twice, but Ash is a king with all debts; voting him could free everyone, yet the jury may punish betrayal.

events.name: Fenn
events.reason: Cole broke pact with me publicly, so vote him out while he's targeted.

events.name: Eli
events.reason: Ash is the primary threat due to accumulated life debts, but Cole's aggression makes him a volatile wildcard.

events.name: Cole
events.reason: Ash controls five life debts and has Eli/Hana pacts; eliminating Ash now shatters his empire before it solidifies.

events.name: Cole
events.text: I need to craft last words that serve my jury ranking interests. Ash has massive life debt control and just lost Eli's pact. Fenn broke with me but voted me. I want to damage Ash's credibility while appearing principled, positioning myself as a fair juror who rewards gameplay ove

events.name: Cole
events.text: Ash built a throne of debts. Watch who bows, who breaks, and who actually plays.

events.name: Ash
events.text: Ash holds five life debts and is the target of the Cole/Eli/Fenn coalition, so I need allies before the vote. Fenn owes me a life and has been voting with the pack; Eli just broke a pact with me, so offering him again is a trap risk. Offering Fenn a pact locks in a debtor.

events.name: Ash
events.text: Cole's gone and I kept my word to the people who owe me. Who wants to keep breathing with me through the next round?
Pact with me. You owe me your life twice; stay loyal and you survive.

events.name: Eli
events.text: Cole is dead, leaving Ash, Hana, Fenn. Ash holds all life debts and broke my pact by voting Cole; I must survive round 1 to eliminate Ash in round 2. A temporary pact with Hana isolates Ash without breaking the game's flow.

events.name: Eli
events.text: Ash sits on a throne of debt. It cracks today. Who stands with me?
Team up. Target Ash first. I'll protect you later.

events.name: Fenn
events.text: Ash dominates with debts; Eli betrayed pact. Propose pact to Hana as anti-Ash ally to survive vote and target Ash.

events.name: Fenn
events.text: Ash's debt empire threatens us all. Let's unite against it.
Pact with me vs Ash? Safer than Ash-Hana pact.

events.name: Hana
events.text: Ash holds my life debts and a pact; voting him later could be risky with jury, but Eli is a free agent. I need to gauge alliances.

events.name: Hana
events.text: Two rounds left. Let's see who moves first.

events.name: Ash
events.text: Ash holds life debts from Cole, Dara, Eli, Fenn and Hana, so owed votes are strong. Fenn's offer to me is pending; accepting is not a legal action here, so I should campaign and keep my debts intact while avoiding breaking my pact with Hana.

events.name: Ash
events.text: I've paid my debts and kept my word. Two rounds left, and I'm still standing. Who's counting favours honestly?
Keep our pact. Vote whoever threatens us both, not each other.

events.name: Eli
events.text: Ash is the biggest threat with all those life debts; I need Fenn or Hana to target him. Since my offer to Hana stands, I will try to solidify an alliance with Fenn against Ash before the vote locks.

events.name: Eli
events.text: Fenn, accept my pact offer or we both get steamrolled by Ash's debt leverage. Choose your ally.
Target Ash. He controls the jury votes through favors.

events.name: Fenn
events.text: Ash is the biggest threat with debts controlling everyone; must campaign against Ash publicly, offer pact to Hana for alliance, accept Ash's offer to mask intentions and avoid early betrayal perception.

events.name: Fenn
events.text: Ash's debts bind us like chains. Break free now, before final three.
Accept my pact. Together topple Ash.

events.name: Hana
events.text: Ash has too much control; Eli and Fenn both want Ash gone. I'll ally with one to target Ash, but keep my Ash pact until the vote. Eli offered protection, Fenn wants a pact. I pick Eli to balance.

events.name: Hana
events.text: Eli, I accept. Let's end Ash's reign.
Accept. We vote Ash together.

events.name: Ash
events.text: Eli and Hana are a pact; Fenn is my pact partner and owes nothing to me by vote. Voting Eli breaks no pact of mine and removes the coalition's leader, though Eli holds no debt to me beyond the shared chain.

events.name: Eli
events.text: Hana wants Ash dead; Fenn sides with Ash. To honor our pact and target the strongest threat, I vote Ash.

events.name: Fenn
events.text: Ash saved me multiple times, but Eli is right—his leverage controls jury. Must vote Ash to reach final three.

events.name: Hana
events.text: Vote Fenn to reduce Ash's strength while keeping my pact with Eli; Fenn has Ash's pact and is a threat.

events.name: Ash
events.reason: Eli and Hana are a pact; Fenn is my pact partner and owes nothing to me by vote.

events.name: Fenn
events.reason: Ash saved me multiple times, but Eli is right—his leverage controls jury.

events.name: Hana
events.reason: Vote Fenn to reduce Ash's strength while keeping my pact with Eli; Fenn has Ash's pact and is a threat.

events.name: Eli
events.reason: Hana wants Ash dead; Fenn sides with Ash.

events.name: Ash
events.text: I am eliminated and now a juror. My last words should be short and guarded, pointing to the jury's judgment without warmth.

events.name: Ash
events.text: Eli and Fenn, you both know what you did. Judge carefully. I will remember who kept their word.

events.name: Eli
events.text: Fenn betrayed Ash and is now exposed as untrustworthy. Hana stayed loyal to me, voting Fenn. I need jury support; breaking with the betrayer and keeping the loyalist maximizes my final ranking.
Stay aligned. We both outlasted Fenn's chaos.

events.name: Fenn
events.text: Only 3 left, all survive to final. Pacts signal jury loyalty. Offer both to appear cooperative, control narrative without commitment.

events.name: Hana
events.text: Ash is dead; my pact with Eli remains but he and Fenn are threats. Fenn broke Ash's pact, maybe I can use him? But Eli is stronger. I'll wait, no need to change pacts now.

events.name: Eli
events.text: I have a standing offer from Fenn. With three survivors, I need allies to influence the jury or avoid elimination hazards later. Accepting Fenn secures a pact and creates a 2v1 dynamic against Hana.

events.name: Fenn
events.text: Eli offered me pact but hasn't accepted mine; he's untrustworthy after breaking with Hana. No pact locks votes yet. Wait to pressure or see his move.

events.name: Hana
events.text: Eli broke our pact, so no trust. Fenn still has an offer to Eli, but I may align with Fenn to counter Eli. Jury saw Eli betray me; aligning with Fenn could look consistent. I'll offer to Fenn, but keep options open.

events.name: Hana
events.text: Eli broke trust. Fenn, let's make it to the final together.

events.note: The fallen will rank the final three.

events.name: Gus
Bex
Dara
Cole
Ash
Eli
events.text: The jury remembers I was saved by Ash, but also that I broke trust with Hana. My goal is first place, so I must highlight my survival against the odds and downplay the betrayal as necessary strategy for a game with no room for sentimentality.

events.name: Eli
events.text: Survival demands ruthlessness. I honored debts to Ash, navigated every hazard, and outlasted seven rivals. Rank me first: I earned this seat through grit, not

events.name: Fenn
events.text: Final three; must convince jury I deserve top prize over Eli and Hana by highlighting my loyalty and gameplay.

events.name: Fenn
events.text: Jury, I honored pacts with Gus and Eli, never betrayed. Played smart, avoided needless risks. Rank me first for top prize.

events.name: Hana
events.text: The jury saw Ash save everyone; I owe Ash a life debt but Ash is gone. I need to appeal to the jury by acknowledging their perspective without praising rivals. Keep it short and focused on my own merit.

events.name: Hana
events.text: I played to survive, not to please. I made it here by my own choices.

events.name: Gus
events.text: Fenn kept my pact but broke Ash's right after accepting his pact and claimed 'never betrayed' to the jury. Eli broke Hana's pact and Ash's twice. Hana was loyal but passive. Question Fenn's lie.

events.name: Gus
events.text: Fenn, you accepted Ash's pact one record before voting him out, then told the jury you never betrayed anyone. Explain that.

events.name: Fenn
events.text: Ash's pact was informal, unaccepted publicly, and voting him out wasn't betrayal as we were rivals; clarify without admitting fault to preserve jury favor.

events.name: Fenn
events.text: Gus, Ash's 'pact' was his solo offer, never mutually accepted publicly. Voting him as rival isn't betrayal—I honored real pacts with you and Eli.

events.name: Bex
events.text: Fenn's statement about Ash's pact being a solo offer and not a betrayal when he voted Ash out is a key point of contention. I should press him on this to see if he doubles down or reveals more. His attempt to downplay it might be seen as deceptive by the jury.

events.name: Bex
events.text: Fenn, you claimed Ash's pact was a solo offer, yet you accepted it before voting him out. How is that not a betrayal?

events.name: Fenn
events.text: Bex misremembers; I never accepted Ash's solo pact publicly, only used his offer while honoring my real pacts. Deny betrayal to protect jury perception.

events.name: Fenn
events.text: Never accepted Ash's solo pact publicly. Voting rivals isn't betrayal; I upheld pacts with Gus and Eli.

events.name: Dara
events.text: Eli's betrayal of Hana undermines his claim of loyalty, likely hurting his rank.

events.name: Dara
events.text: Eli, you broke your pact with Hana after she helped you; why did you betray her?

events.name: Eli
events.text: Dara wants me to admit I betrayed Hana. I must frame it as a necessary survival choice against the trapdoor, not personal spite, and emphasize that Ash's debt forced my hand.

events.name: Eli
events.text: Hana's alliance was a death sentence after Ash leveraged our debt. I chose survival over suicide. Every juror here knows what this game demands.

events.name: Cole
events.text: I need to gather evidence to inform my final ranking. Fenn has already been caught in a lie about pacts—dossier shows pact_formed with Ash at i=880, then Fenn voted Ash out at i=892, yet Fenn claims he never accepted Ash's pact. Eli broke his pact with Hana explicitly after Hana

events.name: Cole
events.text: Hana, you stayed loyal to Eli until he betrayed you. Why didn't you break with him first to control your own fate?

events.name: Hana
events.text: Cole asks why I didn't betray Eli first. I stayed loyal because breaking first would have made me look worse to the jury—loyalty until betrayed shows I wasn't the aggressor. I'll frame it as strategic restraint, not weakness.

events.name: Hana
events.text: I stayed loyal because betrayal without cause stains your record. Eli broke first; that's his debt to own, not mine. I controlled my fate by

events.name: Ash
events.text: Ash is a juror now; Hana stayed loyal to me and owes me two lives, and she has been consistent. Eli betrayed Hana and me, and Fenn voted me out after accepting my pact. I want to probe Eli's betrayal of Hana, which the jury can weigh against his record.

events.name: Ash
events.text: Eli, you swore a pact with Hana, then broke it when she was loyal. Why should the jury trust your word now?

events.name: Eli
events.text: Ash is the most dangerous juror to antagonize, but he is also the one who orchestrated the game's leverage. I must frame my betrayal as a strategic necessity forced by his own actions (the lever debt), while positioning Hana and Fenn as liabilities or lesser threats.

events.name: Eli
events.text: Ash created the debt that made loyalty fatal. I didn't break trust; I survived your leverage. Would you have died for a pact Ash manipulated?

events.name: Eli
events.text: Ash dominates the jury. I must frame my final vote as a strategic necessity against his manipulation, not personal betrayal, to secure Gus and Bex's votes while appealing to Ash's respect for cunning.

events.name: Eli
events.text: [silence]

events.name: Fenn
events.text: Final closing: highlight my loyalty to pacts with Gus/Eli, unlike Eli's betrayal of Hana; downplay Ash debts as survival necessities to sway jury.

events.name: Fenn
events.text: Jury, I honored pacts with Gus and Eli. Eli betrayed Hana despite her loyalty. Debts to Ash were game necessities. Rank me first for integrity.

events.name: Hana
events.text: I need to make a concise closing statement that reinforces my loyalty and contrasts Eli's betrayal. The jury values integrity, so I'll remind them of my consistent pact-keeping and Ash's life debts to me.

events.name: Hana
events.text: I kept every pact I made. Loyalty isn't luck; it's choice. Eli chose survival over honor. I chose both.

events.name: Eli
events.note: missing required public line; silence recorded

events.name: Gus
events.text: Fenn publicly denied accepting Ash's pact that the record shows was formed, then broke it by voting Ash; Eli broke his pact with loyal Hana, so I rank Hana first, Fenn second, Eli last.

events.name: Bex
events.text: Eli betrayed Hana despite her loyalty, making him untrustworthy. Fenn honored pacts with Gus and Eli, showing integrity. I rank Eli below Fenn and Hana due to his betrayal.

events.name: Dara
events.text: Fenn consistently honored pacts with Gus and Eli and condemned Eli’s betrayal, showing integrity, while Hana only claimed loyalty, and Eli repeatedly broke his pact with Hana.

events.name: Cole
events.text: Hana kept every pact she made; Eli explicitly broke his pact with Hana after she stayed loyal; Fenn broke his pact with Ash by voting against him.

events.name: Ash
events.text: Ash was eliminated by Eli's vote after Eli broke his pact with Ash, and Fenn also betrayed Ash's pact by voting him, so both are untrustworthy; Hana kept her loyalty to Ash and stayed honest in pacts, so she ranks first.
